harness: extension/scripts/build-firefox.mjs + npx web-ext lint (web-ext 10.7.0, extension/ devDependencies) + selenium-webdriver/geckodriver (scratchpad, not committed)
notes: extension/scripts/build-firefox.mjs reads extension/manifest.json and extension/background.js but never writes to them -- it only writes into extension/dist/firefox/. Verified: both source files' mtimes (background.js 2026-09-26 15:02, manifest.json 2026-09-27 14:36) predate this build run (2026-09-27 15:06+), matching the pre-existing working-tree diff from before this task started. Chrome behaviour (extension/*, unpacked as-is) is byte-for-byte unchanged.

background.js gets exactly one Firefox-only patch: a 10-line capability check inserted as the first statement of ensureOffscreenDocument() (`if (typeof chrome === 'undefined' || !chrome.offscreen) return;`). Diffed and confirmed -- nothing else in the 1617/1627-line files differs.

manifest.json changes: permissions drops 'offscreen' (Chrome-only, no Firefox equivalent); background.service_worker -> background.scripts:['offscreen.bundle.js','background.js'] + type:'module' (Firefox MV3 event page; module type required because background.js uses static ES import); browser_specific_settings.gecko added {id:'dhristi-privacy-agent@sih26171.dev', strict_min_version:'128.0' -- the floor set by content_scripts[].world:'MAIN' on shadow-detect.js}. host_permissions and content_security_policy (incl. 'wasm-unsafe-eval') carry over untouched.

Firefox inference path: offscreen.bundle.js (same bundle Chrome loads inside chrome.offscreen, unmodified, not rebuilt) is loaded as a second background script so it runs in the SAME event-page document as background.js. Firefox event pages have a real DOM/WASM/OffscreenCanvas, so its existing chrome.runtime.onMessage listener for DETECT_OBJECTS is already registered by the time anything calls detectObjects() -- no iframe, no second page, no change to offscreen.entry.js's source.

DETECT_OBJECTS routing capability check: hasOffscreenDocument() already returns false safely on Firefox unmodified (chrome.runtime.getContexts doesn't exist there); the only Firefox crash site was the unconditional chrome.offscreen.createDocument(...) call inside ensureOffscreenDocument(), now guarded as described above. Chrome's code path is completely unaffected by the guard (chrome.offscreen is truthy there).

steps_that_worked: npm install selenium-webdriver geckodriver in a scratch dir (background, logged).
geckodriver npm wrapper downloaded geckodriver v0.37.1 (background) and started a WebDriver server on 127.0.0.1:4444 successfully.

steps_that_failed.step: selenium-webdriver Builder.forBrowser('firefox').usingServer('http://127.0.0.1:4444') with options.setBinary() pointed at the Store Firefox alias
steps_that_failed.error: InvalidArgumentError: binary is not a Firefox executable
steps_that_failed.cause: The Microsoft Store package's firefox.exe is an App Execution Alias into a sandboxed WindowsApps package tree; geckodriver's binary validation rejects it even though the shell can launch it directly.

steps_that_failed.step: Download+silent-install a standalone Firefox to get a geckodriver-compatible binary
steps_that_failed.install_attempt_1: FirefoxSetup.exe /S /InstallDirectoryPath=<scratchpad>\install, run from Git Bash: exit code 0 but no files were written under the target directory -- most likely a path-separator mangling artifact of invoking a native NSIS installer from MSYS bash with a mixed backslash/forward-slash path, not conclusively diagnosed.
steps_that_failed.install_attempt_2: FirefoxSetup.exe /S (default location) via PowerShell Start-Process -Wait: killed by Claude Code's own background-process low-memory protection before it could complete ('system is running low on memory' -- explicitly not a command/script failure). Per the harness's own instruction on that signal, this was not retried automatically.
